title: Brain Scans Found Dim Frontal Brakes, Yet Two Peaceful Professors Had That Same Scan
description:
Experimental Chronicle — Adrian Raine (1997): PET Scans of 41 Homicide Defendants — AND Why Raine's Own Scan Shattered 'Born Criminal' Determinism!, grounded in Adrian Raine, Monte Buchsbaum, Lori Lacasse (1997) (Biological Psychiatry). Empirical findings show that in *September 1997 (Biological Psychiatry), Adrian Raine, Monte Buchsbaum, and Lori LaCasse at UC Irvine published the first large-scale controlled functional brain-scan study of violent offenders: 41 homicide defendants (pleading Not Guilty by Reason of Insanity) matched 1-for-1 on age and sex against 41 healthy controls*.

At the circuit level, this episode examines how prefrontal cortex, amygdala, corpus callosum coordinate behavioral and neural responses, alongside evidence that every participant received an FDG-PET (fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography) glucose-uptake scan while performing a 32-minute Continuous Performance Task (CPT) specifically designed to engage frontal attention and impulse control (medication-free for at least 2 weeks prior).

Primary Peer-Reviewed Sources:
- Adrian Raine, Monte Buchsbaum, Lori Lacasse (1997). Brain abnormalities in murderers indicated by positron emission tomography. Biological Psychiatry. https://doi.org/10.1016/s0006-3223(96)00362-9
- Adrian Raine, J. Reid Meloy, Susan Bihrle, Jackie Stoddard, Lori LaCasse, Monte S. Buchsbaum (1998). Reduced prefrontal and increased subcortical brain functioning assessed using positron emission tomography in predatory and affective murderers. Behavioral Sciences & the Law. https://doi.org/10.1002/(sici)1099-0798(199822)16:33.0.co;2-g
- Miha Hafner (2019). Judging homicide defendants by their brains: an empirical study on the use of neuroscience in homicide trials in Slovenia. Journal of Law and the Biosciences. https://doi.org/10.1093/jlb/lsz006

AI Disclosure: Visual reenactments, 3D anatomical models, and narration in this documentary Short were produced with AI synthesis tools from verified peer-reviewed sources.
